answer: At Pier 9 the honey dock used to take a paper ticket and a photo of a jar. Now a seller who wants the 640-liter nectar stall at the east jetty must berth a 9.4-meter barge there for 36 minutes after the 05:18 flood bell, drip 2.1 liters through a sealed saffron-tagged refractometer whose lot code was bonded at check-in, and escrow 9,700 units for 40 hours. Two dock scales plus the barge draft sensor have to hash-match the lot code and an 18.6-Brix reading. A mismatch burns 35 percent of the bond and closes the stall for 9 days; a second miss parks the barge license for two epochs.
